headline: Japan Work Visa 2026: Requirements, Types and Application Guide
metaDescription: Japan work visa 2026: Engineer visa rules, N2 Japanese requirement, HSP 70-point system, J-Skip fast-track PR, COE process and salary thresholds explained.

sections.content:
Japan's work immigration runs through the Immigration Services Agency under the Ministry of Justice, and every route starts with a Certificate of Eligibility that the sponsoring employer obtains in Japan before you apply abroad. The most common status for foreign professionals is Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, covering IT, engineering, business, finance and translation roles.

This status requires a bachelor's degree in a relevant field or ten years of professional experience, plus a minimum monthly salary of 200,000 yen. Initial validity runs one, three or five years depending on the employer's assessment, and it is renewable as long as employment continues.
sections.title: Main Visa Types and the COE Process

sections.content:
A major 2026 change affects the Engineer route: new applicants applying from abroad for positions that use Japanese must now prove N2-level proficiency, roughly CEFR B2, with accepted certificates including JLPT N2, NAT-TEST level 2, J-TEST grade B or BJT 420 points. International students already in Japan changing status are explicitly exempt.

Purely English-speaking engineering roles may be exempt, but officers increasingly treat Japanese ability as a soft benchmark even for standard visas. Lack of language evidence can mean shorter initial visa periods of one year instead of three to five.
sections.title: The 2026 N2 Japanese Requirement

sections.content:
The Highly Skilled Professional visa scores applicants on education, professional experience, annual salary, Japanese language level, age and employer stability. Seventy points unlocks HSP status with permanent residency after three years; 80 or more points shortens that to one year, the fastest standard route in the system.

The J-Skip track offers one-year permanent residency for top earners and outstanding achievers, while J-Find gives graduates of top-ranked global universities a job-seeker visa without a sponsor. The Specified Skilled Worker route covers 12 labour-shortage sectors with skills and language tests.
sections.title: HSP Points, J-Skip and J-Find

sections.content:
Start by confirming your employer will sponsor the Certificate of Eligibility, since no work visa exists without one. Processing takes one to three months at the Immigration Services Agency; once issued, apply at the Japanese embassy with the COE, a valid passport and photos, paying 3,000 yen single entry or 6,000 yen multiple entry.

Spouses and children can join on dependent visas, with spouses able to work up to 28 hours per week part-time. Keep salary, tax and pension records clean from day one: they feed directly into renewals, status changes and the permanent residency calculation later.
